text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Bjoern Rune Gjelsten, head of Aker RGI, will take over as new chairman of the board of Aker Maritime and says Aker Maritime will follow an aggressive line in the future with large acquistions to double the company's turnover.
- Experts in the currency market can't see any clear explanations why the Norwegian crown has been weakened by 2.5 percent compared to the German mark in the last two days.
- While 4,000 Norwegian patients are sent abroad for treatment, there is capacity to treat 6,300 patients in private hospitals in Norway.
- Airline Braathens SAFE, Europay Norway and IBM launched the first secure payment system over the Internet across national borders on Thursday.

- A suggestion for a new gas directive from the EU has endangered investments for 170 billion crowns in the Norwegian continental shelf. Under the proposal, oil companies will not be able to sign long-term sales agreements with gas customers in the European Union.

- EU's proposal for a new gas directive may put a stop to Saga Petroleum ASA's development of the Kristin field. Without the opportunity to enter long-term agreements with gas buyers in Europe the risk will be to high.
